headline.purpose: The page header's title line — bilingual, Khmer first, then " · English" in soft ink only when the two differ.

title.purpose: A Section heading and a dialog title.

body.purpose: Form fields, prose, button labels, card copy — carries most of the interface.

label.purpose: Emphasis text that isn't a heading — a price card's product name.

caption.purpose: Metadata, chip text, table cells, the page header's date line. Line height 1.6 for Khmer.

figure.purpose: Not a size but a treatment: any number a person compares to another number, via Roboto's own tabular figures with a slashed zero, never a separate mono face.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The dialog panel — the one thing in the system that floats above an inert page.

shadows.name: scrim-dialog
shadows.purpose: The dialog overlay, darkening the page behind it.

shadows.name: tab-active
shadows.purpose: The active tab on a boxed TabsList, lifting it off the tray.

shadows.name: sidebar-active
shadows.purpose: The active sidebar menu item's ground.

shadows.name: sidebar-outline
shadows.purpose: The sidebar's outline button variant, a hairline drawn as a shadow so it doesn't shift layout on hover.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The one focus ring in the system, keyboard-only via :focus-visible.

motion.name: slide-up
motion.value: opacity 0 → 1 with translateY(8px) scale(0.98) → none, 200ms ease-out

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: The skeleton sweep while data loads.

motion.name: state-colors
motion.purpose: Every hover, press and selection change on buttons, rows and chips. Ground shifts, never a lift.

motion.name: sidebar-width
motion.purpose: The sidebar expanding and collapsing between its full and icon-rail widths.

motion.name: picker-indicator
motion.purpose: The native date field's calendar glyph waking on hover.

narrative.overview:
CKD Ticket is not its own visual world. It is the second application built to the same convention as CKD POS, sharing that system's floor (`#F5F6F8`), its cool white surfaces, its one hairline, its amber family mark, and its four semantic marks — the same numbers, defined in the same variable names, in both codebases. Where the till sells food across a counter, this app sells entry, memberships and coupons across a different counter for the same club; the owner asked, twice, that they read as one company's software rather than two designers' opinions, and the token layer is the mechanism that makes that literal rather than aspirational. A future agent extending either app inherits this system by default; a deliberate divergence is a decision to record here, not a shortcut to take silently.

This is the app's second visual identity. Its first attempt — a "Gym Whiteboard" of chalk-board surfaces, marker-weight type and four hue-coded magnets — was built, reviewed, and rejected outright; every trace of it (the board grid, the magnet vocabulary, `components/board/`) has been deleted from the codebase, and none of it is recorded below. What replaced it is conventional admin software played straight: a page header, a filter row, cards, a table. The craft is in the execution, not the invention — legible Khmer at counter distance, one committing action per screen, and a data table dense enough to hold a full day's sales above the fold on a 1366×768 laptop.

Two adjustments separate this build from its sibling, and both are Khmer-legibility commitments rather than taste: `--ink-soft` sits at 38% lightness here, darker than POS's 46.9% annotation, because Khmer's thinner strokes and stacked diacritics need the extra contrast to hold 4.5:1 at caption size; and the compact table's line height is 1.6 rather than a Latin-tuned 1.4, so a stacked Khmer consonant cluster doesn't crowd the row beneath it. Both are noted at their point of use below, not treated as a second design language.
keyCharacteristics: Shares `--floor`, the amber pair and the four semantic marks with CKD POS byte-for-byte — one design system, two codebases
Paper-white surfaces on the same cool grey floor, separated by a single 1px hairline
One accent (amber `rgb(217 123 42)`) confined to the committing action, lettered in ink because white fails contrast on this ground
Facilities demoted from a colour system to a quiet 8px dot beside a name; the price itself is always ink
Four semantic marks — paid, pending, void, notice — one chip, one set of tones, matching POS's
Roboto + Nokora, bundled locally; every comparable figure is tabular with a slashed zero
`--ink-soft` held at 38% lightness and the caption line height at 1.6, both tuned for Khmer where POS's Latin-tuned values would fall short
36px controls, a 48px header, compact ledger tables — one density step down from POS's touch-first 40px/56px, because this is a seated laptop counter, not a standing tablet

rules.name: The Amber Confinement Rule
rules.body: Amber marks one thing: the committing action, or a selected option standing in for one (the busy price card, mid-sale). It carries ink lettering, not white — white measures 3.1:1 on this amber and fails the contrast floor; ink measures 5.8:1. Disabled amber is never a faded amber; it is the wash ground with soft-ink text, because a faded accent under a pale label is unreadable exactly when the seller is deciding whether they can take the money. Audit test: point at any amber pixel and name the sale or approval it commits; if you can't, it's wrong.

rules.name: The Quiet Facility Rule
rules.body: A facility is a name with an 8px dot beside it, drawn from `lib/facility.ts`, and nothing more. It does not stripe a card, ground a tile, or colour a price — a swim ticket's price is ink, exactly like a gym ticket's, because gym's green and steam's orange do not clear 4.5:1 against white and a system that let facility colour carry the figure would be quietly inaccessible on its two most common products. The dot exists so a queue of prices reads left-to-right by colour before anyone reads the label; it stops there.

rules.name: The Ink-Soft-at-38 Rule
rules.body: `--ink-soft` is fixed at 38% lightness in this app, not the 46.9% CKD POS uses for the equivalent role. Khmer's thinner strokes and stacked diacritics read this system's secondary text at caption size constantly — a page header's date line, a table's row-number column, a chip's muted tone — and POS's lighter value would land at 4.6:1 where this one holds 6.58:1. This is the one deliberate divergence in the shared neutral ramp, made once in `index.css` rather than overridden per component.

rules.name: The Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number a person compares to another number — a price, a count, a time, a page number — carries the `.figure` utility: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero` plus the matching `font-feature-settings`. CKD POS routes the same category of number through JetBrains Mono; this app deliberately does not. A generic monospace gives a decimal point a full character cell, so `$1.50` renders as `$1 . 50` at display size — tried and rejected here. Roboto's own tabular figures with a slashed zero give the column alignment the treatment exists for, without a third bundled face and its network-free-fonts cost.

rules.name: The Caption-at-1.6 Rule
rules.body: The `caption` type step sets its line height at 1.6, not a Latin-tuned 1.4. Khmer stacks a subscript consonant (coeng) and below-vowels beneath the baseline; at 1.4 those marks crowd the descenders of the line below. The system's compact table cells go further still, to a hand-tuned 19px, for the same reason.

rules.name: The Khmer-First Header Rule
rules.body: `PageHeader` renders a page's title in Khmer first, with the English name following after "·" in soft ink only when the two strings actually differ. The counter reads Khmer; the owner reads either; nothing here defaults to English and demotes Khmer to a subtitle.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Shadow means "this is floating above the page and the page beneath it is inert." Nothing at rest carries one; the dialog is the only surface that does.

rules.name: The One Chip Rule
rules.body: Record state renders through `Chip` with one of the four tones, or through `StateDot` when a label would repeat itself. No screen hand-rolls a badge with its own padding, radius or colour pair.

rules.name: The One Table Rule
rules.body: Every list of records — sales, prices, requests, reports — renders through `DataTable`. A page does not lay out its own `<table>` with its own header styling.

rules.name: The One Access Table Rule
rules.body: `lib/access.ts` is the only place a role's reach is decided. The sidebar's visible menu, the dashboard's quick actions and report links, and any future admin-only control all call `visibleMenu` or `canReachPath` against the same `MENU` table, so the menu and the rest of the app cannot disagree about what a role may do. An unresolved role (missing, blank, a retired name like "Kiosk") resolves to `null` and reaches nothing, rather than guessing.

rules.name: The Paper Slip Rule
rules.body: The printed slip (`components/ComponentToPrint/`) is paper, not screen: it sets its own explicit `Roboto, Nokora` font stack, and its layout is drawn in literal black-on-white — `text-black`, `border-black`, `bg-black` — rather than through `ink`, `rule`, `paper` or any other screen token. A thermal printer needs true black rules that won't fade and a fixed font declaration independent of whatever the screen's token layer does next; the slip is deliberately not wired to this system so that a future token change here can never silently soften a receipt.

dos: Do treat CKD POS's token names as the shared contract — `--floor`, `--amber`, `--paid`/`--pending`/`--void`/`--notice` and their tint/deep steps carry the same numbers in both apps. Extend the pair together when a value must change.
Do confine amber to the one committing action on a screen, lettered in ink.
Do put a facility's identity through `lib/facility.ts` — a dot and a name — and keep prices in ink regardless of facility.
Do route every state through `Chip`/`StateDot` and every record list through `DataTable`.
Do mark every comparable number with `.figure`.
Do keep `--ink-soft` at 38% and the caption line height at 1.6 in this app; they are Khmer-legibility floors, not stylistic choices to relax.
Do read and write role access exclusively through `lib/access.ts`.
donts: Don't stripe a card, a column, or a price with a facility colour. The dot names it; the ink prices it.
Don't put a white or chalk label on the amber ground — the label is ink, and disabled amber is wash-on-soft-ink, never a fade.
Don't invent a fifth state colour, or route a comparable number through anything but `.figure`.
Don't wire the printed slip to screen tokens; it stays literal black-on-white with its own explicit font stack.
Don't put a shadow on anything at rest — only the dialog floats.
Don't reintroduce a board, a magnet, a marker weight, or any other trace of the app's first ("Gym Whiteboard") identity; it was reviewed and rejected, and nothing about it is a fallback.

Don't diverge from CKD POS's shared tokens without recording why here and in POS's own DESIGN.md — the two are meant to read as one company's software, and a silent drift defeats the point of sharing the layer at all.
